reason: The text passage (1 Chronicles 11) portrays elite groups very favorably. The elders (זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל - ziqnei Yisra'el) of Israel are shown as unified, recognizing David's legitimate leadership and formally covenanting with him, establishing him as king according to God's word. The 'mighty men' (הַגִּבּוֹרִים - ha-gibborim), who constitute the military elite, are celebrated for their courage, strength, and remarkable feats in battle. These warriors are presented as heroes whose deeds brought about God's deliverance. The narrative structure consistently validates the elite's decisions and actions, presenting their alignment with David and God's purposes as righteous and praiseworthy.
